title: [project] Spectral Sun - in-engine cinematic
author: Massive-Edge-1266
selftext:
Hi! I got inspired by all the videos of people building game drafts with Opus 5.5, three.js and WebGL. I’ve always wanted a desert world where you can just be: wander, explore, and uncover the untold stories of lost civilizations. That’s how "Spectral Sun" started :)

The first generations with Claude were already impressive but full of simplifications and shallowness. Then I wanted real Rayleigh scattering. Then clouds... Then wind, and echoes in the ruins. Then more detailed 3D models and used Meshy... and it started to roll :D

Basically, with some for artistic-sake assumptions, all based on real physics laws

Real star catalog, seen from \~100 light-years toward Orion (Hypparcos - HYG catalogue, you can see real constellations how they would look like from planet in this region); two suns, and an alien air mix that changes the sky’s colour

Eye adaptation, night vision without colour, glare from bright lights

The crystal burst: the flash’s light curve, the shock front from a precomputed fluid sim, debris glowing as black bodies and cooling as they fly, smoke trails dispersing by turbulence law

Lightning, dust storms, sand that flows like granular matter

Tools:

\- Claude Code with Opus 5.5 - code, tests, rendering, sound mixing. (organized with my custom plugin in multisession orechestration - several Claude Code sessions working in parallel - one acting as an orchestrator, others - implementers, reviewers, judge, sender and so on)

\- GPT Image Gen 2 for visual references

\- Meshy for models

\- Blender for final refinement, adjustments (done by Claude)

\- Suno for music.

Consider this as in-engine cinematic, with a bunch if mistakes and simplifications rendered offline on a rented GPU.

So work in progress, it's not representation of current gameplay but uses a lot of elements from it

I’d love to hear your feedback - what works, what doesn’t, what you’d want to explore in a world like this? :)
